newsitem.title: USA: NY State, Washington review NYNEX merger.
newsitem.headline: NY State, Washington review NYNEX merger.

text.p: State Attorney General Dennis Vacco met the Justice Department's antitrust regulators Friday to discuss the federal and state reviews on Bell Atlantic's $23 billion proposed takeover of NYNEX Corp.

Vacco, who opposes the deal on anti-competitive grounds, confirmed he had a meeting with the Justice Department's top antitrust enforcer, Joel Klein -- just a few days before government antitrust lawyers are expected to announce their decision.

The attorney general declined to discuss details of the meeting, deferring to issues he raised in an April 7 letter to John O'Mara, chairman of the New York State Public Service Commission (PSC), which approved the proposed deal on March 20 with 10 conditions -- none of which Vacco suggested to replace competition lost by the merger.

"Following an extensive investigation and review of confidential company documents and other evidence, I concluded that the proposed merger would likely have an adverse impact on competition in New York telecommunications markets, particularly for residential and small business users," he said. "I also found that, if approved as proposed, the merger would not only be likely to deprive New York local telephone service markets of a significant new entrant Bell Atlantic, but might entrench Nynex's existing monopoly over local service and tend to impede the development of competition in new and emerging telephone service."
In the letter, Vacco restated the three conditions he wanted before the deal was approved by the PSC.

The first is auctioning off the wireless assets Bell Atlantic and Nynex already own together for cellular phone service to another purchaser to open up competition in business and residential markets.

The second is requiring the merging firms to demonstrate that competition has taken root in New York local telephone markets before they can provide long distance service within their territories under the 1996 Telecommunications Act.
The third requirement is an agreement to pro-competitive pricing rules for new entrants into the state's telephone markets, which need access to Nynex's facilities.

Vacco also asked the PSC to impose stiffer penalties against Nynex for failing to meet service standards and chided state regulators for failing to impose rate reductions for residential and small business customers in connection with the proposed merger calling on the Commission to push now for lower rates.

"In my view, however, the only real impetus for Nynex to improve its abysmal service record would be the presence of vigorous competitors that could provide a real alternative for consumers dissatisfied with the present monopoly provider," he said.
